item.title: Tom Homan's Bold Moves: ICE at Airports, DHS Shutdown, and the Battles Ahead
item.description:
What happens when the agency responsible for airport security runs out of money — and the government’s top immigration enforcer steps in to fill the gap? That’s exactly the scenario playing out across the United States right now, and Tom Homan is at the center of it all.

Key Takeaways

  • Border czar Tom Homan confirmed ICE officers are being deployed to U.S. airports to assist TSA during the ongoing DHS shutdown.
  • TSA workers have gone unpaid since DHS funding lapsed on January 31, causing massive staffing shortages and long lines.
  • Homan rejected Democratic demands for ICE agents to remove masks, citing an 8,000% increase in death threats.
  • Democrats and Republicans remain deadlocked over DHS funding, with no resolution in sight after more than 40 days.

Tom Homan and the ICE Airport Deployment

On March 23, 2026, Tom Homan confirmed on CNN’s State of the Union that Immigration and Customs Enforcement agents would be deployed to U.S. airports starting the following day. The move came after President Donald Trump announced plans to send ICE officers to help ease the chaos caused by severe TSA staffing shortages.

item.title: TSA Agents Government Shutdown: The Airport Crisis Explained
item.description:
What happens when 480 airport security officers quit and thousands more stop showing up to work — all while millions of Americans are trying to fly? That’s not a hypothetical. It’s happening right now across U.S. airports as the Department of Homeland Security shutdown stretches past 40 days.

Key Takeaways

  • More than 480 TSA officers have quit since the DHS shutdown began on Feb. 14
  • TSA callout rates have more than doubled, from a normal 2% to over 6.1% nationwide
  • Roughly 60,000 TSA employees have gone nearly a month with reduced pay and received $0 paychecks
  • Wait times at some airports have exceeded three hours
  • President Trump ordered DHS to “immediately pay” TSA agents on March 26
  • TSA leadership warns of “long-standing” negative impacts even after funding is restored

TSA Agents Hit a “Breaking Point” as Paychecks Dry Up

The partial government shutdown, triggered when DHS funding lapsed on Feb. 13, has left roughly 60,000 TSA employees working without pay. As of this week, TSA staff prepared to miss a third consecutive paycheck, receiving $0 pay stubs — a gut punch for workers already under intense stress.

item.title: MSP Airport Spring Break Chaos: TSA Wait Times, Staff Pressure, and What Travelers Need to Know
item.description:
Spring break 2026 is hitting MSP Airport hard. With thousands of travelers flooding Minneapolis-Saint Paul International, TSA employees are under mounting pressure — yet security lines keep moving. Here’s everything you need to know before heading to the airport.

Key Takeaways

  • Spring break travelers are packing MSP Airport, driving significant volume increases
  • TSA employees face growing pressure amid federal workforce uncertainty, but lines keep moving
  • Current TSA wait times at MSP remain manageable despite the surge
  • MSP also making headlines in managed service provider (MSP) industry with major deals

MSP Airport Spring Break Rush — What’s Happening on the Ground

According to KARE 11, spring break travelers are packing MSP Airport as of March 2026. The annual surge has turned terminals into a sea of families, college students, and vacationers all competing for overhead bin space.
